case_reviews.reviewer_assessment: Both CCAP PDFs place the text under Tris preparation. It is an instruction fragment, not an ingredient, and current wording does not recover an acid identity. Nonchemical-token disposition is supported.

Three TOGO primary JSONs retain500g fat-free beef and boiling/skimming/filtering into particles plus filtrate. A generic beef-extract alias would collapse a tissue preparation; per-recipe scope is appropriately retained.
NBRC1284 itself prints six waters and400mg. Neither a familiar trihydrate nor frozen400g/L is authoritative. Source correction requirement is specific and justified.

JCM631 has14.45g MgSO4.7H2O,4.42g CaCl2.2H2O,vitamins andMetals44, distinct from29.7/3.335g Hutner recipes. Nominal list and KOH/pH boundary are correct; list completeness is not chemical-ID completeness.
TOGO M2422 and2423 both explicitly expand YE to yeast extract and cite the GSY mixture context. The narrow alias addition does not assign a branded extract or chemical structure.
TOGO M2553 gives lowercase2m and no concentration-unit metadata. Retaining the solution scope without silently choosing molarity or molality is appropriate.

Original recipe text says cysteine hydrochloride hydrate but lacks stereo/water count; the linked GMO label adds L/monohydrate without independent source wording. Holding exactCHEBI91248 is justified.
JCM1267 acidified10% solution differs from NBRC239 solid formula row andTOGO3240 weighed salt. A universal exact alias would collapse stock and solute contexts; source splitting is necessary.
JCM552 explicitly L-cysteine.H2O.HCl, with553/627 inheritance not changing this solute. A raw spelling alias is supported, while whole-owner holds and separate stock use remain intact.
NBRC1116 generic sodium EDTA lacks sodium count; GMO disodium label is an interpretation. Distinct sodium/hydrate owners cannot resolve that omission; precise product requirement is justified.

TOGO2570 directly lists10mL of2.5% L-cysteine-HCl under separately prepared reducing stocks. Percent basis and water state are unreported. No pure-solute equivalence or final-medium concentration is claimed.
JCM520 and95 retain L-malate but no Na count; the S-specific disodium owner and its DL contamination cannot supply missing stoichiometry. Holding source assignment is sound.

TOGO3149 original-method text retains cysteine-hydrochloride without stereo/hydrate. Issue905 is contextual caution, not proof of this source identity; the decision correctly requires direct reagent evidence.

TOGO2554 comments explicitly add powdered sulfur separately and exclude sodium sulfide from basal preparation. Seven listed basal inputs are supported despite broader source table rows; source gas/preparation remains separate.

Captured Carini2014 method prints NaPHO3.5H2O at1micromolar. One-sodium versus dibasic identity is unresolved; preserving published formula rather than correcting by chemical expectation is warranted.
Both frozen1992-linked recipe records carry content-bound NaMoO4.2H2O versus laterNa2MoO4.2H2O hold. Failed paper retrieval confers no permission to repair or borrow the later source.
TOGO2885 specifies0.1M HCl as1L trace-stock solvent input. Nominal source-qualified acid solution is supported; unreported solvent composition should give UNKNOWN completeness.
JCM1051 explicitly supplies0.1M L-cysteine.HCl.H2O10mL. Exact solute form is preserved and no pure-solute replacement is proposed; completeness must reflect unreported stock formulation.
TOGO2575 names L-cysteine.HCl.H2O as12.5g input within reducing solution. Component nesting does not make the name the whole solution; hydrate-owner raw alias is appropriate.
NBRC1507 names0.1M Tris/HCl pH7.5 with no acid/base ratio. Proposed total Tris-moiety concentration correctly avoids assigning0.1M separately to both acid and base.
TOGO2596 uses1M HCl within sludge preparation. Reagent strength and variable addition are distinct; source-qualified stock is supported with unknown full composition.
JCM552/627/1098/707/757 retain L-sodium lactate. The double hyphen is lexical; rejecting D,L on an L owner is justified by stereo distinction and does not validate unrelated legacy aliases.
JCM87 explicitly offers20% lactic acid or1–6N HCl to pH5.6. This is an alternative titrant preparation; stereochemistry and percentage basis remain unspecified.
DSM600 enumerates the artificial seawater salts with1000mL water input; proposed absolute quantities avoid a fabricated final-volume denominator and preserve CaCl2/SrCl2 hydrate ambiguity.
DSM330 haemins preparation uses1mL1N NaOH before dilution. Normality is retained as reagent strength; no automatic pure-solid or final-medium concentration assertion is made.

TOGO2228 identifies five basal-broth inputs before horse/swine serum addition; Solution1 is a nested BHI/PPLO/Hanks preparation. Proposed boundary correctly excludes final sera and avoids BHI identity collapse.

DSM600 explicitly referencesDSM590. That source retains malformed molybdate and approximateKOH7.3g; literal nominal recipe is supportable, but the draft omitted the approximate KOH amount and misused PARTIAL.
NBRC1022 confirms sodium tetrathionate family, not tetrathionate ion or water state. The unresolved exact supplied salt is a valid requirement, not an excuse to use the ion owner.
TOGO2598 raw one-water cysteine-HCl lacks stereo even though GMO calls itL. The label narrows hydration but does not establish L identity.
TOGO2313 independently lists citrus-peel and apple pectin as alternatives. Tissue scope is material; a broad pectin candidate is defensible without assigning a generic exact product.
NBRC1397 gives magnesium glycerophosphate0.5g without isomer,hydrate or supplier. Sodium-glycerophosphate issues are analogous cautions only; magnesium-specific evidence is still required.

ExactSigmaA9647 product evidence supports current heat-shock/pH7/lyophilized supplied form. The owner already preserves the catalogue; retaining fraction terminology as product scope avoids a redundant unsafe generic alias.
DSM1165 has one ammonium, DSM1148 two; twelve waters do not decide iron valence. The five aggregate occurrences cannot share one corrected salt without occurrence-specific source correction.
NBRC1196 explains Substrates* with selectable vanillic/syringic-acid examples. It is a recipe parameter, not fixed material or union owner.
JCM979 stock excludes the separately listed vitamins and retains malformed molybdate. Source explicitly saysKOH about7.3g; draft omission and completeness misuse must be corrected.
Normalized sodium nitrilotriacetate wording does not choose Na stoichiometry or hydrate. The exact trisodium monohydrate proposal for55 is not evidence for this generic source.
NBRC302/305 themselves printO3. Source-level oxygen count cannot be repaired from similarity to molybdateO4; matching inherited spellings are not independent confirmation.

JCM900 nominal stock differs fromJCM631 and includes its own malformed molybdate. Shared B nominal-stock proposal is acceptable only with actual cross-case backlinks and preserved approximateKOH amount.
Dithionate versus dithionite changes oxidation state/oxygen count. With directJCM876 unavailable, historical wording must remain unresolved rather than inferred from reductant role.
FrozenTOGO3115 reports0.1M but directAPI/solution6187 retrieval fails; a comparative0.1N source does not establish this exact stock lineage. Preserve unresolved primary preparation.

JCM704/JCM833-lineage source wording is sodium citrate dihydrate. Initial exact trisodium inference needed independent conventional-name support beyond the ontology label; author is supplying supplier nomenclature evidence, without assigning the source a vendor product.
All three DSMZcell-culture recipes name100x amino acids but omit catalogue/list. No individual amino acid or arbitrary commercial blend may replace the mixture.
NBRC1333 prints four waters in1000x stock and0.1g per100mL. Four-water source must remain distinct from common dihydrate; stock dilution does not repair supplied form.
CCAPWalnes PDF givesMnCl2.4H2O in the nutrient solution. Correcting this occurrence’s damaged subscripts/letterO is independently supported, without a global malformed synonym.

FrozenTOGO2653 stock label is25%sodium acetate, direct primary attempts failed. The source-qualified percent preparation cannot be interpreted as pure acetate or assigned a percentage basis by convention.
NBRC989 gives25mL50%sodium lactate, while frozen derivatives disagree units. Retain the volume correction lead separately from unknownstereo/percentage basis; no averaging.

findings.summary: Approximate KOH7.3g omitted from stock payloads though explicit in bothprimaryrecipes. Preserve approximate amount in notes, not as exact finalconcentration.

PARTIAL enum misused for unresolved chemicalIDs or unreported fullstock. COMPLETE means complete sourceconstituentlist; PARTIAL means explicitlyomitted additionalcomponents; UNKNOWN meanssource doesnot establishcompleteness.
